solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Producers (i - b):** Green plants are producers as they produce their own food through the process of photosynthesis.
 
• **Primary Consumers (ii - d):** Herbivorous animals are primary consumers because they feed directly on producers (plants).
 
• **Tertiary Consumers (iii - a):** Carnivorous predators are tertiary consumers as they feed on primary and secondary consumers.
 
• **Decomposers (iv - c):** Bacteria are decomposers that break down dead organic material and recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Producers:**

 
 
• Producers are organisms that can make their own food using light, water, carbon dioxide, or other chemicals.
 
• They form the base of the food chain.
 
• Examples include green plants, algae, and certain bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Primary Consumers:**
 
 
• Primary consumers are herbivores that feed on producers.
 
• They occupy the second trophic level in the food chain.
 
• Examples include cows, rabbits, and insects that eat plants.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Consumers:**
 
 
• Tertiary consumers are predators that feed on secondary consumers.
 
• They occupy the highest trophic levels in the food chain.
 
• Examples include lions, eagles, and sharks.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Decomposers break down dead or decaying organisms, and in doing so, they carry out the natural process of decomposition.
 
• They play a crucial role in recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• Examples include bacteria, fungi, and certain insects.
